families.name: Pro Fixed spray nozzles (Pro-Spray fixed arc)
Pro-Spray fixed arc nozzles, 240 and 270 degree (TT/TQ) - 2016 catalogue only
MP Rotator (standard: MP1000, MP2000, MP3000, MP3500, MP Corner)

notes: SOURCES. Hunter's current sites (www.hunterirrigation.com, www.hunterindustries.com) answered every automated request with 403, so the US cut sheets were read from Hunter's own legacy file host d7.hunterindustries.com (same CA-Cutsheet-*-US.pdf files; PDF dates Nov 2021 to Oct 2022). The numbers were cross-checked against older Hunter catalogue pages held by distributors: Pro Fixed (dripdepot.com, 2016 catalogue pp. 61-63), Pro Adjustable (dripworks.com, 2015 catalogue pp. 56-58), MP Rotator (sprinklerwarehouse.com, 2018 catalogue pp. 42-44), MP800 (nelsonirrigation.com, 2019 cut sheet), MP design guide (dripdepot.com, 2016). Every value common to two editions agrees, except the trajectories noted below.

FULL-CIRCLE GPM. For flow = 'arc' families every row's gpm is the full-circle equivalent: the printed gpm x 360 / the arc of the chart row used, rounded to 3 decimals (e.g. 12Q 30 psi 0.67 x 4 = 2.68; 12TQ 2.00 x 4/3 = 2.667). radiusFt and chartPrecip are as printed for that same row.

PRO FIXED: the chart offers no 5T (use 4A/6A), no 17T or 17F (use 17A); the 2016 catalogue also lists 5/8/10 TT and TQ and 17 TT/TQ as 'use 4A/6A, 8A, 10A, 17A'. chartPrecip at 30 psi (the chart's bold recommended pressure). Trajectory of the 8 series: 15 deg in the 2022 cut sheet, 0 deg in the 2016 catalogue; 15 used.

PRO FIXED TT/TQ (12TT, 12TQ, 15TT, 15TQ, family hu-pro-fixed-tt-tq) appear only in the 2016 catalogue chart (distributor copy); the 2022 Hunter cut sheet lists Q, T, H, F only, so these may be discontinued. Their rows are the 2016 numbers.

PRO ADJUSTABLE: rows are the chart's 360 deg rows; arcMin 0 / arcMax 360 as the chart says ('Adjustable from 0 to 360'), though its rows start at 45 deg. chartPrecip from the 360 deg row at 30 psi. Flow is close to proportional to arc for 8A, 10A, 12A, 15A, 17A (within 5%), NOT for 4A worst 42% (45 deg, 40 psi: 0.16 gpm = 1.28 full-circle vs 360 deg row 0.9); 6A worst 24% (45 deg, 25 psi: 0.17 gpm = 1.36 full-circle vs 360 deg row 1.1). Each Pro Adjustable nozzle also carries printedByArc (every arc table the chart prints, 45 to 360 deg, gpm AS PRINTED for that arc, not full-circle), the field heads.js rowAtArc reads. The 4A/6A printed precipitation also changes with arc (4A at 30 psi: 4.81 to 6.26 in/h square). Trajectory of 8A: 15 deg in the 2021 cut sheet, 0 deg in the 2015 catalogue; 15 used. The chart notes that the PRS30 regulates to a maximum of 30 psi and that the radius screw may need adjusting to reach catalogue radius and flow.

PS ULTRA: its cut sheet's 'standard nozzles' chart (8A, 10A, 12A, 15A, 17A) is number-for-number the Pro Adjustable chart (checked), and its strip table is SS-530 (the spec builder calls the factory-fitted strip '5SS'). So a PS Ultra with a preinstalled nozzle uses hu-pro-adjustable or hu-st-ss-530; the body still takes any female-threaded nozzle.

STRIPS (hu-strip, hu-mp-strip): flow = 'constant' because a strip nozzle has no arc; gpm is as printed for the whole pattern. The charts give width x length, not radius, so radiusFt is null and each row carries the printed widthFt and lengthFt (fields beyond SCHEMA.md). Neither chart prints a precipitation rate, so chartPrecip is null. LCS/RCS corner strips are written as type 'end' with corner 'left'/'right', the encoding rainbird-sprays.json uses (the head sits at a corner of the rectangle). arcFixed is null (the charts print no arc for strips).

MP ROTATOR is matched-precipitation and stored as flow = 'arc'. The chart prints rows at several arcs per model; the stored full-circle gpm comes from ONE row per model: the 180 deg row x 2 for the 90-210 deg models (MP1000-90, MP2000-90, MP3000-90, MP3500-90, MP800SR-90, MP815-90), the 270 deg row x 4/3 for the 210-270 deg models (-210), the 360 deg row for -360 models, and the 90 deg row x 4 for MP-CORNER (45-105 deg). chartPrecip is from that same row at 40 psi (the chart's optimal/bold pressure). The adjustable MP nozzles also carry printedByArc with every arc row the chart prints for them, gpm as printed for that arc: -90 models 90/180/210, -210 models 210/270, MP-CORNER 45/90/105. The chart does not say whether its 210 deg row belongs to the -90 model (at its maximum) or the -210 model (at its minimum); it is given to both. The chart gives no trajectory (null). MP1000 and MP Corner (45 deg) print '--' at 25 psi, so those nozzles have no 25 psi row.

MP ROTATOR ARC SPREAD (other arc rows of the same nozzle differ from the stored full-circle value by more than 5%, at 40 psi): MP2000 90 deg row at 40 psi implies 1.72 gpm full-circle vs 1.54 stored (from the 180 deg row); MP3000 90 deg row at 40 psi implies 3.44 gpm full-circle vs 3.64 stored (from the 180 deg row); MP3500 90 deg row at 40 psi implies 5.12 gpm full-circle vs 5.72 stored (from the 180 deg row); MP800SR 90 deg row at 40 psi implies 0.92 gpm full-circle vs 0.84 stored (from the 180 deg row); MP800SR 210 deg row at 40 psi implies 0.737 gpm full-circle vs 0.84 stored (from the 180 deg row); MP815 90 deg row at 40 psi implies 1.96 gpm full-circle vs 1.86 stored (from the 180 deg row). Every other MP model's arc rows agree within 5%. MP800SR 210 deg row: its GPH column (e.g. 29.4 GPH = 0.49 gpm at 40 psi, i.e. 0.84 full-circle) agrees with the 180 deg row, so the 210 deg GPM column may be the misprint.

PRO FIXED proportionality (full-circle equivalent vs the series' F nozzle, more than 5% apart at 30 psi): 10Q at 30 psi: 1.68 gpm full-circle vs 10F 1.59; 10T at 30 psi: 1.71 gpm full-circle vs 10F 1.59; 10H at 30 psi: 1.76 gpm full-circle vs 10F 1.59. This is as Hunter prints it: the 10F's own printed precipitation (1.53 in/h square) is lower than the 10Q/T/H (1.63 to 1.69).

MP800SR: the chart has MAX RADIUS and MIN RADIUS columns. Rows hold the max-radius values; minRadiusFt and minRadiusGpm (full-circle equivalent of the MIN RADIUS flow column) are added to each MP800SR row (fields beyond SCHEMA.md). The 800 cut sheet says the minimum radius setting is reached at 30 psi (PRS30) and nominal at 40 psi (PRS40). MP815 has no min-radius columns.

MP800 CHART INCONSISTENCY: its GPH column disagrees with its GPM column in several rows; GPM was transcribed. MP800SR 90 deg 35 psi: 0.21 GPM vs 11.4 GPH (= 0.19 GPM); MP800SR 210 deg 30 psi: 0.35 GPM vs 22.2 GPH (= 0.37 GPM); MP800SR 210 deg 35 psi: 0.38 GPM vs 26.4 GPH (= 0.44 GPM); MP800SR 210 deg 40 psi: 0.43 GPM vs 29.4 GPH (= 0.49 GPM); MP800SR 210 deg 45 psi: 0.45 GPM vs 31.8 GPH (= 0.53 GPM); MP800SR 210 deg 50 psi: 0.49 GPM vs 33.6 GPH (= 0.56 GPM); MP800SR 210 deg 55 psi: 0.56 GPM vs 34.8 GPH (= 0.58 GPM); MP800SR 360 deg 30 psi: 0.66 GPM vs 37.8 GPH (= 0.63 GPM).

MP CORNER DOUBT: the MP Corner flows as printed (e.g. 0.39 gpm at 90 deg, 14 ft, 40 psi; the MP1000 at the same arc and radius prints 0.21) work out to about 0.77 in/h head-to-head square, yet the same cut sheet badges the MP Corner '0.4 in/hr' and prints no precipitation column for it. The 2016 design guide prints the same flows. Transcribed as printed; treat MP-CORNER precipitation with suspicion.
MP ROTATOR radius reduction: up to about 25% on all models (cut sheet); the chart rows are at full radius.

BODIES: every Pro-Spray, PRS30, PRS40 and PS Ultra body is listed as taking all seven families, since each cut sheet says 'Compatible with all female-threaded nozzles'. Hunter's recommended pairing: PRS30 with Pro Fixed / Pro Adjustable / strip nozzles (30 psi), PRS40 with MP Rotator (40 psi; PRS30 for MP minimum-radius settings). Pro-Spray (unregulated) operating range 15-100 psi (PRS30/PRS40 the same inlet range); PS Ultra 20-70 psi, not regulated. Not included: PROS-00 shrub adapters, the side-inlet -SI variants of the 6" and 12" bodies (same hydraulics), and MP Rotator 'HT' male-threaded nozzles.

Body pop-up heights are the cut sheets' 'Pop-up height' (PROS-03 3", PROS-04 4", PROS-06 6", PROS-12 12"; PSU-02 2", PSU-04 4", PSU-06 6"). PSU-06 and the PS Ultra side strip: the 5SS strip is offered on 2" and 4" models only.
